# Best travel chargers with multiple USB-C ports

**Best overall: UGREEN Nexode 100W (3× USB-C + 1× USB-A)**
- One port delivers the full 100W alone. With two devices it splits to 65W and 30W, and with all four ports in use it's 45W, 30W and 10.5W on the remaining ports ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026)).
- Downsides: at 8.3 oz it's the heaviest of the group, and no cable is included.
- Android Central also names it the best 100W charger ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger)).
- Where to buy: I don't have a direct product link. The "Check price on Amazon" buttons are on [TechWise's review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026).

**Best compact: Anker Prime 67W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A)**
- It weighs 4.78 oz, and either USB-C port can deliver the full 67W alone. It stays at 65W across two devices and about 64.5W across three.
- It also supports PPS for Samsung and Pixel phones.
- Downside: only two USB-C ports.
- Where to buy: see the Amazon button in [TechWise's GaN charger guide](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026).

**Best for a power-hungry laptop: Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A)**
- It has the most headroom of the three, but power is still shared once several devices connect.
- Where to buy: see [TechWise's roundup](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026).

**Best value: Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A), 2-pack for $49.99**
- Each charger gives 65W from either USB-C port alone. With two devices it splits 45W and 20W, and it has foldable prongs.
- Downside: the laptop port drops to 45W when other devices are plugged in. That's fine for a MacBook Air, but not full speed for a 65W laptop.
- Buy: [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W 2-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u). This is an affiliate link, and no discount code applied when it was last tested.
- Don't confuse it with the "GaN5 Pro Flat 65W," which has only one USB-C port ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026)).

## Tips
- **Plug adapters:** All of these have US prongs, so you'll need a plug adapter abroad but not a voltage converter. If you'd rather have swappable plugs built in, [Android Central's travel adapter guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel) lists the Epicka TA-105 (75W, 3× USB-C) and the UGREEN 65W Nexode travel adapter (2× USB-C).
- **Port sharing:** Put your laptop on the highest-power USB-C port, and add phones and earbuds after it.
- **Cables:** Use a 5A e-marked cable for anything over 60W, or the cable will limit the charger.

If you tell me what you're charging, such as a laptop model, phone, or tablet, I can narrow this to one pick.
